posts.style: Design & Aspiration · The Lap Pool Between the Houses
posts.alt: A Carlsbad Mediterranean backyard at golden hour: a long narrow pool with a raised stone-veneer spa and copper water bowls, ivory porcelain paver deck, a bronze louvered pergola over an outdoor kitchen with a built-in grill and a lit fire table, olive trees, lavender and agave, with neighboring tile-roof homes visible close by on both sides
posts.hook: A narrow lot isn't a smaller yard. It's a yard that has to be drawn with more care.
posts.caption:
Carlsbad lots are rarely wide. The temptation is to shrink everything to fit. The better answer is to give the yard one clear axis and let every piece line up with it.

Here the pool runs the length of the lot, with the spa raised at the near end and two copper water bowls sounding at the far corner. The kitchen and fire table sit under a single louvered pergola at the end of the line of sight, so the whole yard reads as one composed view from the house. Ivory porcelain keeps the deck cool underfoot and the palette quiet, and olive and lavender soften the edges against the neighboring walls.

The selections:
• Belgard Porcelain pavers in ivory
• Eldorado Stone veneer spa wall
• Bobe copper water bowls
• StruXure louvered pergola in bronze
• Lynx built-in grill & Warming Trends fire table
• olive, lavender & agave · FX Luminaire lighting

We build pools. The shell is a licensed subcontract, like every other trade on the job, so you hold one contract and one firm accountable.

posts.style: Neighborhood · Driveway & Curb Appeal · The Cobble Drive
posts.alt: The front of a two-story Spanish-style tract-luxury home in Sunbow, Chula Vista, at golden hour: a wide driveway of warm grey-brown Belgard Cobble-pattern pavers with a charcoal soldier-course border and a narrow turf strip, a matching walk to an arched entry, stone-veneer raised planters with an olive tree, agave, sago palms and kangaroo paw, bronze path lights, neighboring tile-roof homes close by on both sides
posts.hook: A driveway doesn't have to be a slab of grey. It can be the first thing about the house you remember.
posts.caption:
Most front yards are asked to do one job: get the car in. This one does three. The drive is laid in a cobble pattern with a dark border that frames it like a rug, a thin ribbon of turf breaks the surface so it never reads as a parking pad, and the walk picks up the same paver to carry you from the curb to the door as one continuous piece.

A stone-veneer planter anchors the garage corner with a single olive and a few agave, and the kangaroo paw on the right gives the one note of warm color that makes it look cared for. Path lights make it as good at 7 PM as at noon.

The selections:
• Belgard Cobble-pattern pavers in a warm grey-brown blend with a charcoal border
• SYNLawn turf strip
• Eldorado Stone veneer raised planters
• olive tree, agave, sago palms & kangaroo paw in decomposed granite
• Kichler bronze path lights

Want the front of your home to say as much as the back? DM “DESIGN”.

posts.style: Process Carousel · Property Walk to Built
posts.alt: Four-slide SDLR process carousel of one La Mesa ranch-home backyard between neighboring houses: the existing yard at the property walk with a cracked slab, a failing old patio cover and dry lawn, the full 3D design render with louvered pergola, outdoor kitchen, fire pit and curving turf, a hand-rendered design drawing of the same layout with client details blurred, and the finished build at golden hour
posts.hook: Here's how a backyard goes from tired to built, without a single guess along the way.
posts.caption:
A yard like this one is ordinary in the best way: a normal lot, close neighbors, a slab that's seen better years. What changes it isn't a bigger idea. It's an order of operations.

Swipe through how our design process works, start to finish:

1. The property walk: we start with what's actually there. The cracked slab, the old cover, the grade, the sun and the fence lines.
2. The 3D design: the whole space modeled so you can see the pergola, the kitchen, the fire and the lawn in place, and change anything before it's real.
3. The drawing: every edge, level and planting resolved on paper so the crew builds exactly what you approved. Client details stay private.
4. The build: and it matches, because nothing was left to be figured out in the field.

The selections:
• Belgard Urbana paver patio
• StruXure louvered pergola
• Eldorado Stone kitchen island with Lynx built-in grill
• stone-veneer fire pit with curved seat wall
• SYNLawn turf · olive, agave & lavender in raised planters

Want to see your own yard in 3D before anything gets built? DM “DESIGN”.

posts.style: Seasonal · Christmas Eve · The Table Under the Lights
posts.alt: A Del Sur backyard terrace at blue-hour dusk on Christmas Eve behind a white board-and-batten modern farmhouse: a charcoal pergola over a long linen-dressed dining table with candle lanterns, a citrus tree wrapped in warm white lights, a single olive-branch wreath on a pergola post, a lit linear fire table with built-in cushioned seating, silver porcelain terrace, stacked-stone walls with agave and grasses, neighboring homes with glowing windows close by
posts.hook: The best Christmas Eve decoration is a yard you actually want to be standing in.
posts.caption:
Tonight the yard doesn't need much. A long table, candles in lanterns, one citrus tree wrapped in warm light, and a single olive wreath on the post. The fire does the rest, and the seating beside it is where the evening goes once the plates are cleared.

Nothing here is seasonal. The terrace, the pergola, the stone walls and the lighting are there every night of the year. December just gives it a reason to be used after dark.

From all of us at San Diego Landscape Remodeling, Merry Christmas to you and yours.

The selections:
• Trex Pergola in charcoal
• Warming Trends linear fire table with built-in seating
• Belgard Porcelain pavers in silver grey
• Eldorado Stone retaining walls
• citrus, agave & ornamental grasses · FX Luminaire uplighting

Imagining your own terrace after dark? DM “DESIGN”.

posts.alt: An Eastlake, Chula Vista family backyard in soft morning light behind a two-story grey stucco tile-roof home: a freeform pool with a raised spa, Belgard Urbana paver deck, a curving turf lawn, a bronze pergola lounge with a stone fire bowl, stone-veneer planters with olive trees and agave, neighboring tile-roof homes close by on both sides
posts.hook: You can't hand a backyard off. Someone has to stay with it from the first walk to the last detail.
posts.caption:
A yard like this has hundreds of small decisions in it: where the lawn curves, how the pool edge meets the paver, which side the fire sits on. Each one is easy to get wrong when the person who drew it isn't the person who's there.

That's why every SDLR project is held by the two of us, Gio and Mike. You're not handed to an account manager or a project coordinator. The person who walks your property is the person who designs it, and the person you call when something needs a decision. It's slower to take on, and it's why the finished yard matches the plan.

The selections:
• Belgard Urbana pavers with stone-veneer coping
• SYNLawn turf with a curved border
• Trex Pergola in bronze
• Bobe fire bowl
• olive & agave in raised planters

Want a yard with someone actually behind it? DM “DESIGN”.
